title: Amateur satellites
blurb: Why a satellite's frequency shifts as it passes, how tracking works, and how to use uplinks, downlinks and beacons.

T8B01.why: Beacon telemetry reports the satellite's **health and status**: things like battery and temperature.
T8B01.trap: Beacons don't report your signal strength or give precise time.

T8B02.why: A transponder is shared. Too much power makes your signal dominate and **blocks access for other users**.

T8B03.why: Tracking programs give the **map, pass times with azimuth and elevation, and Doppler-corrected frequency**. All three.

T8B04.why: Amateur satellites carry **SSB, FM and CW/data**. No single mode is the only one.

T8B05.why: A beacon is a **satellite transmission carrying status information**.
T8B05.trap: It isn't an antenna, light, or reflector.

T8B06.why: A tracking program needs the **Keplerian elements** that describe the orbit. Power and Doppler history aren't inputs.
T8B06.trap: Doppler is an output the program calculates, not something you feed in.

T8B07.why: Doppler shift is an **observed frequency change from relative motion** between satellite and station.
T8B07.trap: It isn't an orbit change or a band-swapping mode.

T8B08.why: U/V is uplink then downlink: **U = UHF (70 cm) up, V = VHF (2 m) down**.

T8B09.why: Spin fading comes from the **rotation of the satellite and its antennas**, which sweeps the pattern past you.
T8B09.trap: Doppler shifts frequency; it doesn't fade strength.

T8B10.why: **LEO = Low Earth Orbit**, close to Earth with a period of about 100 minutes.

T8B11.why: Amateur satellite telemetry is not encrypted, so **anyone** can receive it.

T8B12.why: Match the beacon: when your downlink is **about as strong as the beacon**, your uplink power is about right.
T8B12.trap: Beacon telemetry doesn't report your signal level. Compare against the beacon instead.
